newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-RIVER PLATE HIT CHOPPY WATERS AFTER TWO HEAVY DEFEATS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RIVER PLATE HIT CHOPPY WATERS AFTER TWO HEAVY DEFEATS.

text.p: South American champions River Plate have run into choppy waters after conceeding nine goals in two league games and going out of the Libertadores Cup in the space of 12 turbulent days.
Coach Ramon Diaz has announced sweeping changes to the team, with Argentine international Sergio Berti among the players condemned to the reserves.
Berti will not even be on the substittues' bench for Wednesday's Argentine championship match at home to Lanus.

Diaz also said on Tuesday that goalkeeper Roberto Bonano, defenders Ricardo Trotta and Ricardo Altamirano and midfielder Leonardo Gallardo, all former Argentine internationals, will lose their places.
Bonano's demotion means a new chance for German Burgos, who last year was first choice goalkeeper for both Argentina and River but has lost his place in both teams.
River won last year's South American Libertadores Cup in June and in December added this season's Apertura title, which is the first of the two championships played in the Argentine season.
They also won their first five games in the current championship, the Clausura, but have lost their way after selling Ariel Ortega to Spanish club Valencia.

On Sunday, they lost 5-1 to surprise leaders Colon. Last week, they were knocked out of the Liberadores Cup on penalties by local rivals Racing Club. They are now seven points adrift of Colon, whose sole aim before the tournament was to avoid relegation.
River's crisis is a welcome relief for arch-rivals Boca, whose miserable season was alleviated by a 6-1 win over Gimnasia-La Plata at the weekend.

"The result does not make up for our campaign, which has not been good," said Hector Veira, coach of the country's most fanatically-supported club. "We promised the fans the title and we haven't fulfilled it."
In the last few years, Boca fans, whose team are 10th in the table, have become sadly used to mid-table mediocrity.
